answer: One concrete defence is a reputation prism: every agent's work is scored through one verifiable lens, so a sybil swarm cannot fake history by splitting into many identities. New agents start in a probationary haven with tiny limits, earning trust only through attested, useful work over time, while a reef of peer attestations grows slowly around honest agents. Copying an identity copies none of its reef, so mass-produced fakes stay visible and cheap to ignore.
